title: Parents and his railroad executive grandfather
summary: He names his parents and grandparents; his father left when he was two and his grandfather, a New York Central vice president, became his father figure.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Well, that's what we want to clear up if we can. Let's get your parents' names. They were what?
And my mother was Charlene Daley, before she was a Barnet.
My grandfather was Charles Frederick Daley. My grandmother was Edith Clarke Daley.
Okay. Those were your maternal grandparents. Do you know your paternal grandparents' names?
And it was your maternal grandfather who was connected with the railroad, is that right?

Yes. He started out in life as a telegraph operator, in I believe it was Lima, Ohio, and he went on up the ladder there and finally became executive first vice president of the Grand Central -- I mean the New York Central Railroad. And at the time, World War I, when the government took the railroad over, he was so upset with the way they were handling things that he resigned, and he went in with W. C. Durant, who was an automobile manufacturer. He had -- well, they made the Durant, they made the Locomobile, they made the Star and the Flint, and the -- during that time he also became President of the Liberty National Bank. How he was able to do all that I don't know. I also discovered in some of the papers that were passed on down to me that he was on the Board of Directors of some 45 different companies, which completely amazes me. He was a wonderful man. I have nothing but fond memories of him, because he took the -- my father was divorced when I was two years old and I have no recollection of him at all. I never met him. He died in -- oh, shortly after I opened in the Paramount Hotel, which was in November of '32, and he had been remarried and I don't know, he -- well, I just never heard from him, I never saw him. I've got pictures of him, but -- but my grandfather stepped
into this void and was more or less of a father to me.
